cards.body:
## Summary
The browser smoke suites are 27 standalone scripts, and each one owns everything itself: the vite preview child, a port picked by hand, a hand-written type for the game's window harness, its own click semantics and its own performance budgets. The copies drift, and nothing catches it. Extract a `packages/tools/src/smoke/` kit and type the harness contract once, in the game. Migrate the live tour (u3-browser, which u4-tour runs) plus d3 and forecast as the proof.

## Description
The drift is already in the tree. u6-tour lost the prop-depth fix u3 received. u1/u2 assert a figure height from before scale contract v3. cf1 and u1 disagree about the signature of `__arena.reset`. Eight ports are each claimed by two suites under `--strictPort`, so suites can't run side by side. Suites that never check `server.exitCode` hide a failed preview behind a 10 s retry loop. The kit has four parts. `preview.ts` takes an OS-assigned port, waits for readiness with a fast fail that carries the server log, and tears down. `driver.ts` holds the canvas-UI verbs every tour reimplements: snap, screen, click (one semantics: wait !busy and enabled, click, wait !busy), pad, visit, train, saveLoad, listenNight, playGames. `checks.ts` holds the pure per-shot assertions: safe area, 64 px targets, D-pad reachability through `nextFocus`, no DOM controls, no overflow. `budgets.ts` is the single source for the fps, CPU p95 and texture ceilings already in the suites; their values are copied, not changed. `packages/game/src/harness-contract.ts` declares `HarnessWindow`. The objects assigned at arena-entry.ts:222 and ui.ts:234 get `satisfies` annotations, so a renamed fixture breaks tsc instead of a 20-minute run.

## Flow
- Write checks.test.ts and preview.test.ts first (cases 1-6). They fail because the modules don't exist.
- Add harness-contract.ts and the satisfies annotations; type-only, no runtime change (case 7).
- Rewrite u3-browser.ts on the kit, which removes about 250 lines of boilerplate. Its screen list, evidence path and browser.json shape stay the same.
- Move d3-widescreen-browser.ts and forecast-browser.ts onto preview + driver.
- npm run gate && npm run build:game. The coordinator runs smoke:u3 / smoke:d3 / smoke:u4 to confirm the evidence JSON is unchanged in shape.

## Expected impact
A new suite is about 60 lines of intent instead of about 300 lines of copy. A harness rename fails at compile time. Any set of suites can run concurrently. A budget change is one edit. The remaining 20 suites can then migrate one per commit, and the u6-tour/u1/u2 clone drift can be retired against a shared driver.

## Evaluation
Claim: the kit makes per-shot checks, port allocation, readiness failure and harness typing single-sourced and testable without a browser.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (no smoke/ module, no HarnessWindow; 8 duplicated ports; 21 Win copies).
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - vitest packages/tools/src/smoke/*.test.ts + tsc (npm run gate), plus npm run build:game for the two game annotations. Smoke runs stay with the coordinator.
Result: better
Gate: architecture

cards.title: `npm run smoke` operator CLI: registry, list/status, safe parallel run, one summary
shared_surfaces: package.json (scripts block only: add `smoke`, keep existing smoke:* as aliases)
acceptance: case 1: registry coverage - the set of packages/tools/src/*-browser.ts, *-tour.ts, *-performance.ts and u6b-audio.ts files -> every file appears in the registry exactly once (today 8 of 27 have any npm entry point; registry does not exist)
case 2: plan(['u3','d3']) -> steps ['build:game', 'u3', 'd3'], with build:game exactly once and no two suite steps sharing a port (today smoke:u3 + smoke:d3 rebuild the game twice)

case 3: plan(['w7-director']) without allowPaid -> throws an Error mentioning 'paid' and 'CAMP_DIRECTOR=claude'; plan(['w7-director'], {allowPaid:true}) -> includes it; plan(['all']) never includes a paid suite

case 4: plan(['camp']) -> refused with status 'retired' and reason naming the missing DOM selector (e.g. '[data-place]'); derived check: for every registry entry whose source uses `[data-` / `#settings-dialog` locators that do not occur under packages/game/src, registry status must be 'retired' (camp, parley, season, w7-scenes, w7-director today)

case 5: status() over a fixture evidence dir with browser.json {passed:true} -> {state:'pass', at:<mtime>}; with a newer browser-failure.json {error:'AssertionError: x'} -> {state:'fail', error:'AssertionError: x'}; no files -> {state:'never-run'}

package.json:25-32 - every smoke:* script prefixes `npm run build:game &&`, so running three suites builds the game three times

packages/tools/src/camp-browser.ts:22,33 - waits for `body[data-ready="true"]` and counts `[data-place]`; season-browser.ts:16 clicks `#settings` / `#settings-dialog`; w7-scenes-browser.ts:28 `#prepare-games`. grep over packages/game/src finds none of `data-place`, `data-visit`, `data-command`, `settings-dialog` (only the canvas button id 'prepare-games' at packages/game/src/screens/chrome.ts:197). These DOM-era suites are silently dead since the canvas camp (u1-browser.ts:147-150 asserts zero DOM controls), and nothing marks them retired

packages/tools/src/w7-director-browser.ts:10 - spawns preview with CAMP_DIRECTOR:'claude' (paid Director calls) and sits next to free suites with the same naming; its only guard is an existsSync on prior evidence (w7-director-browser.ts:6). config.md 'Never touch / never run' requires CAMP_DIRECTOR to stay offline

packages/tools/src/u3-browser.ts:764-773 and u1-browser.ts:642-651 - each suite writes its own failure artifact (browser-failure.json, failure.json, d3-failure.json at d3-widescreen-browser.ts:770, art-browser-failure.json in u4-browser.ts) under its own wave dir; no surface answers 'which suites pass right now'
packages/tools/src/w7-gallery.ts:5-14, u4-gallery.ts:2-25, u6c-gallery.ts:2-27 - galleries are per-wave hand lists, not reading a registry
cards.rollback: Purely additive: new smoke/ files plus one `smoke` script in package.json. Reverting the single commit removes the CLI and leaves all smoke:* scripts and suite files untouched.
cards.runner_up: A cross-wave evidence index (`smoke status --html`) that replaces the per-wave hand-coded galleries (u3/u4/u6c/w7-gallery) with one page that reads the registry and each suite's browser.json.
cards.body:
## Summary
The person running the smoke suites has no surface. There are 27 scripts and 8 npm entries, plus env flags that are documented only in source. Five suites silently target a DOM camp that no longer exists. One suite makes paid Director calls and is named like the free ones. Every run rebuilds the game, and pass/fail is scattered across about 15 wave folders. Add `npm run smoke` backed by a registry: `list`, `status`, `run <suites|all>` with build-once, collision-free ports, a paid-call refusal and one summary table plus exit code.

## Description
`registry.ts` declares each suite: id, file, evidence dir, env profile, surface (canvas|dom), status (live|retired with reason), and paid. It sits on top of the files, not inside them, so it adds nothing to Slot A's write set. A registry test cross-checks the source tree, so a new suite can't be added unregistered. A second derived check finds DOM locators absent from packages/game/src and forces 'retired'. That way a dead suite is visible in `list` instead of failing 20 minutes into a run. `plan.ts` turns a request into steps: build:game once; skip retired suites with their reason; refuse paid suites unless `--allow-paid`; run suites as child processes, serially by default, with `--parallel N` once the Slot A kit provides free ports. `status.ts` reads each evidence dir (browser.json vs the newer *failure.json, mtime) and reports pass / fail (first error line) / never-run. `cli.ts` prints a table and writes `.smoke/last-run.json` (gitignored). The command is the operator's one place to answer 'is the browser surface green, and what do I run next'.

## Flow
- Write registry.test.ts, plan.test.ts and status.test.ts first (cases 1-7). They fail because the modules don't exist.
- Write registry.ts by reading each suite's header and env flags. Mark camp/parley/season/w7-scenes/w7-director retired or paid with the cited reason.
- Write plan.ts and status.ts as pure functions over the registry and fs fixtures.
- Write cli.ts: list | status | run; existing smoke:* scripts stay as aliases.
- npm run gate. The coordinator does one live `npm run smoke -- run u3 d3` to confirm the summary.

## Expected impact
The operator no longer has to know file names. Running N suites goes from N builds to one. The paid Director path can't be started by `all`. Dead suites are labelled instead of discovered by failure. 'What passes now' is one command instead of opening about 15 JSON files.

## Evaluation
Claim: the registry, planner and status reader make the smoke surface listable, safe and summarised without running a browser.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (no registry; 8 of 27 suites reachable by npm; 5 DOM-era suites unmarked; paid suite unguarded beyond an existsSync).
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - vitest packages/tools/src/smoke/{registry,plan,status}.test.ts over fs fixtures (npm run gate); no Playwright in the test path.
Result: better
Gate: direction
